strings.ah_ai: **The AI:** inside Claude the assistant is Claude itself, a real AI model that sees your screen and numbers and can fill in fields. On the website you can connect a free Gemini key in Settings. Without one, the app's own personal model answers, offline too.
strings.ah_design: **Design and theme:** Settings → Display and language → Look. Pick one of 14 designs and a color theme there. Quicker: the palette button at the top. A theme colors any design; "By device" brings back the design's own colors.
strings.ah_hol: **Holiday effects:** holiday themes come with effects such as flags and fireworks, snow and lanterns. Turn them off in Settings → Display and language → Look → Holiday effects. Automatic switching to the holiday theme can be turned on there too.
strings.ah_lang: **Language, currency and country:** Settings → Display and language → Language and region. Choose the interface language, display currency and country of origin there; picking a country also offers its currency. The עב / عر / EN buttons at the top switch language too.
strings.ah_live: **Live data:** rates update in real time. Turn them off with the "Live updates" switch on Home, or search "market data" in Settings. With them off you see the previous trading day's closing rate, with its date. The round arrow at the top refreshes everything.
strings.ah_pdf: **Share and PDF:** under the result on every calculator there are Copy, Share and PDF buttons. Saved files can also be downloaded or shared from the Saved folder.
strings.ah_reset: **Clearing and reset:** the round arrow at the top of a calculator resets that screen. "Clear all" in the save bar deletes what was saved. Single files are deleted in the Saved folder. To reset the whole app: Settings → System → Data and reset.
strings.ah_saved: **Saved:** every save makes a file in the Saved folder (the bookmark icon). Each file can be opened, downloaded, shared or deleted at once. With automatic saving each calculator keeps one file that updates itself.
strings.ah_sep: **Separators:** Settings → Display and language → Numbers. Choose the thousands separator (comma, dot, space, apostrophe or none) and whether to group digits while you type.
strings.ah_what: **What's in the app:** dozens of financial calculators for Israel: salary and the full payslip, tax, mortgage and loans, savings and compound interest, pension, investments, currencies and live rates, real estate and more. There's also a Saved folder, sharing and PDF, 14 designs, holiday themes, three languages and this assistant. Tap a calculator on Home, or ask me which one fits you.

strings.kb_avgcost: When you buy an asset in several rounds at different prices, the average cost is total invested divided by units. Investing a fixed amount monthly spreads timing risk.
strings.kb_betterment: Tax on the gain from selling a home or land. Sellers of a sole residence can be exempt under certain conditions.
strings.kb_boi: The rate the Bank of Israel sets about eight times a year to cool or boost the economy. It drives prime, mortgages and the interest you earn on deposits.
strings.kb_brackets: Israeli income tax is progressive: each slice of income is taxed at its own bracket rate. Moving into a higher bracket only raises tax on the part above it, not on your whole salary.
strings.kb_breakeven: The volume or revenue at which a business exactly covers all its costs. Above it, you start making a profit.
strings.kb_btl: Payroll deductions that fund benefits (unemployment, maternity, disability, old age and more) and the health system. The rate is low on the first part of your pay and higher above it.
strings.kb_capgain: Tax on the real gain from selling shares, funds, crypto and other assets — usually 25%. Losses can be offset against gains in the same year.
strings.kb_compound: When earnings are added to the principal and start earning too. The longer the time, the bigger the effect — so starting early matters far more than the deposit size.
strings.kb_cpi: A monthly index from the Central Bureau of Statistics that tracks prices of a basket of goods and services. "CPI-linked" loans and savings are updated by it.
strings.kb_credit: A credit or instalment deal with interest adds cost to a purchase. Check the effective rate and the total you will pay before agreeing.
strings.kb_crypto: Digital currencies like Bitcoin whose prices swing widely. In Israel, gains from selling or swapping them are subject to capital gains tax.
strings.kb_debt: Two common methods: the "snowball" pays the smallest debt first for momentum; the "avalanche" pays the highest-interest debt first, saving more interest.
strings.kb_div: Part of a company's profit paid out to shareholders. In Israel it is usually taxed at 25%, and 30% for a major shareholder.
strings.kb_effective: The true yearly cost of a loan, including fees and payment frequency. It is the right way to compare offers from different banks.
strings.kb_emergency: Cash set aside for emergencies, usually 3–6 months of expenses, so a lost income or a sudden bill does not push you into debt.
strings.kb_equal: Each month you repay the same share of principal plus interest. Payments start high and fall over time, and total interest is lower than with Spitzer.
strings.kb_fire: Saving and investing hard to reach financial independence and retire early. A common rule of thumb: build 25 times your yearly spending (the "4% rule").
strings.kb_gross: Gross is pay before deductions. Net is what reaches your account after income tax, National Insurance, health tax and the pension contribution.
strings.kb_hishtalmut: A medium-term savings fund your employer pays into, usually available after 6 years. Up to a ceiling its gains are free of capital gains tax — one of the most worthwhile savings.
strings.kb_infl: A general rise in prices over time. With 3% inflation, ₪100 buys next year roughly what ₪97 buys today — so money that is not invested loses value.
strings.kb_lease: Renting a car for a fixed term with a monthly payment. Compare the full cost, including any down payment and end-of-term payment, with buying in cash or on finance.
strings.kb_leave: Paid days off that build up with seniority and job scope. Unused days are paid out when the job ends.
strings.kb_linked: In a CPI-linked loan the balance is updated by the price index. With inflation, the debt and the payment grow even if the rate is fixed.
strings.kb_mortgage: A home loan secured by the home itself. In Israel it is usually built from several tracks, each with its own rate and linkage.
strings.kb_networth: Everything you own (savings, investments, home) minus everything you owe (mortgage, loans). The best measure of your finances and progress over time.
strings.kb_notice: How far in advance whoever ends the employment (employee or employer) must give notice. It depends on seniority and on monthly versus hourly pay.
strings.kb_pension: Mandatory retirement savings: you and your employer put a share of your salary in every month (including a severance part), and it is invested until retirement. Low management fees make a big difference to the final amount.
strings.kb_points: Points that lower your monthly income tax. Each point has a fixed value updated every year, given for residency, gender, children, a degree, army and reserve service and more. Enter yours in the personal profile in Settings.
strings.kb_prepay: A fee the bank may charge when you repay a loan early, mainly on fixed-rate tracks when market rates have fallen since you took it.
strings.kb_prime: The base rate Israeli banks charge on loans. It is always the Bank of Israel rate plus 1.5%, so when the Bank of Israel changes its rate, prime and every loan tied to it change right away.
strings.kb_purchase: Tax paid when buying a home or property. A sole home has lenient brackets; investors and additional homes pay more.
strings.kb_rate: The official exchange rate the Bank of Israel publishes every business day. Banks, exchange offices and card companies add a margin, so the rate you get differs a little.
strings.kb_refi: Replacing your current mortgage with a new one on better terms. Compare the interest saved with the early-repayment fee and costs.
strings.kb_rental: Residential rent has three options: exemption up to a monthly ceiling, a 10% track on gross income, or regular bracket tax with expenses deducted. The calculator compares them.
strings.kb_rentbuy: Comparing renting and investing your equity with buying on a mortgage. The answer depends on interest rates, the alternative return on your money and house-price growth.
strings.kb_reserve: Active reservists can get extra credit points based on the days they served the previous year. Enter the days in the personal profile in Settings and the calculation includes them.
strings.kb_savegoal: An amount you want to reach by a certain date. The calculator shows how much to put aside each month, allowing for returns and inflation.
strings.kb_selfemp: An exempt dealer charges no VAT and has a yearly turnover cap; a licensed dealer charges VAT and offsets VAT on expenses. Both pay their own income tax and National Insurance.
strings.kb_severance: Usually one month's salary per year worked, for an employee who was dismissed and in some cases one who resigned. Part of it is tax-free up to a ceiling.
strings.kb_spitzer: A repayment method with a fixed monthly payment. At first most of it is interest; later most of it reduces the principal.
strings.kb_switched: Language switched to match your keyboard
strings.kb_tracks: The main tracks: prime (floats with prime), fixed unlinked, fixed CPI-linked, and variable every five years. A good mix balances a stable payment against total cost.
strings.kb_vat: A tax added to most goods and services. In Israel it is 18% (since January 2025): price with VAT = price × 1.18, price before VAT = price ÷ 1.18.
strings.kb_yield: The gain from an investment as a percentage over a period. An average yearly return lets you compare investments held for different lengths of time.

strings.n_ap: Use = power in watts × hours. Air conditioners and fridges do not run at full power all the time, so this is an upper estimate. Home tariff from July 2026: 63.52 agorot per kWh incl. VAT.
strings.n_be: Fixed costs and variable cost per unit are assumed constant. Tax counts only if you enter a tax rate.
strings.n_bnMat: 2026 estimate: maternity pay = pay in the 3 months before birth divided by 90, up to 1,752.33 ₪ a day. Full entitlement of 15 weeks (105 days) after working 10 of the last 14 months or 15 of 22, and 8 weeks after 6 of 14. If better, 6 months divided by 180 is checked too. Income tax and contributions are deducted.
strings.n_bnUn: 2026 estimate: daily pay = last 6 months of pay divided by 150, and the benefit is tiered (lower rates under 28). Cap: 550.76 ₪ a day for the first 125 days and 367.17 ₪ after. Monthly figure uses 25 days. Income tax and contributions are deducted, and there are waiting days at the start.
strings.n_capital: Rates: securities gains 25% (30% for a substantial shareholder), dividends 25%/30%, deposit interest 15% and other interest 25%. Surtax: 3% on total income above ₪721,560 plus 2% on its capital part. Foreign withholding and other offsets are not included.
strings.n_cb: 2026 benefit value: 2.48% of the list price a month, up to a price cap of 596,860 ₪. Monthly reduction: hybrid 580 ₪, plug-in 1,150 ₪, electric 1,380 ₪. The value is added to taxable income, so the cost is how much your net pay drops. The Tax Authority has a simulator for exact figures.
strings.n_cc: Interest is computed monthly on the balance. Actual terms depend on the issuer and transactions.
strings.n_cl: Prices as published by the carriers (checked {d}). Carriers offer no public live price feed, so the developer updates the list on the server and the app picks it up. Check the terms before switching. Sources:
strings.n_da: Fees count if you enter them; tax on profit is not included. Averaging lowers your break-even price but does not guarantee a profit.
strings.n_div: Dividends are computed on shares held at the start of each year. With reinvestment, shares are bought at the year-end price. Tax rates are examples; actual withholding depends on the account type and the country of the share.
strings.n_dp: Avalanche saves the most interest; snowball gives quick wins. A cleared debt’s payment rolls to the next. Fixed rates, no indexation or fees.
strings.n_ds: The real price per item helps compare deals. For example, 1+1 equals 50% off only if you really need both.
strings.n_ec: 2026 rates: employer National Insurance 4.51% up to 7,703 ₪ and 7.6% above, pension 6.5% and severance 8.33% (or 6% by agreement). Recreation pay, vacation and sick days are already part of pay and not added.
strings.n_ec2: Net is for a single job without benefits, car or extra credits. For a full payslip use the salary calculator.
strings.n_ev: Petrol price for October 2026: 8.27 ₪ a liter self-service. Home electricity from July 2026: 63.52 agorot per kWh incl. VAT. Public charging costs more. Depreciation, insurance and fees are not included.
strings.n_fi: The safe withdrawal rate is a research rule of thumb, not a promise, and depends on markets, longevity and tax. Capital needed = yearly spending divided by the rate. Deposit and return are held constant.
strings.n_fl: Assumes 9 holidays a year and 2026 self-employed income tax and National Insurance: 52% of the National Insurance part (not health) is deducted from income, and the National Insurance base is worked out the way Bituach Leumi does. Credit points are as you entered them. Pension deposits are not included, so add them to expenses.
strings.n_fr: Order: debts, then emergency fund, then investing up to the target (yearly spending divided by the withdrawal rate). All surplus goes to the current stage. Return is constant; inflation, tax and changing spending are ignored. A roadmap, not a forecast.
strings.n_gd: How it works: a good loan buys something that earns or grows faster than its interest – a business, an income property, study that raises pay. A bad loan funds spending or an asset that loses value – you pay interest and end up with less. The true cost is not just the interest but also what the payments would have earned if saved. Compounding works both ways – in investing it builds for you, in consumer debt it builds for the bank.
strings.n_inFuture: An estimate using the fixed inflation rate you chose. Actual inflation varies year to year.
strings.n_inPast: Based on the official CBS December-to-December change in the consumer price index. The current year uses the latest published index. For exact month-by-month linkage, use the index linkage calculator.
strings.n_inReal: Real return = (1 + return) ÷ (1 + inflation) − 1. Before tax and fees.
strings.n_ins: The comparison is about money only. Before choosing, also check the policy terms: exclusions, waiting period, how a claim is defined, and service. To see your existing policies: the Insurance Mountain on the Finance Ministry site.
strings.n_ins_accident: Personal accident: check what counts as an accident and whether sport is covered.
strings.n_ins_business: Business: employer's liability, third party, equipment and loss of income – each with its own limit.
strings.n_ins_car3rd: Third party: check the cover limit for damage to others' property.
strings.n_ins_carcomp: Car comprehensive: also compare the young-driver deductible, assessor, replacement car and glass.
strings.n_ins_carmand: Compulsory: the cover is the same at every insurer; only the price differs.
strings.n_ins_critical: Critical illness: pays a lump sum on diagnosis; check the list of illnesses and the waiting period.
strings.n_ins_dental: Dental: check yearly caps and the waiting period for big treatments.
strings.n_ins_disability: Disability: an "own occupation" definition is better; part of the cover may already be in your pension fund, so check to avoid paying twice.
strings.n_ins_health: Health: check overlap with your health fund's supplementary plan; one policy per cover is enough.
strings.n_ins_homecontent: Contents: list jewellery and computers separately, and check for new-for-old cover.
strings.n_ins_homestruct: Structure: insure for rebuilding cost; in a shared building check what common property is covered.
strings.n_ins_life: Term life: a variable premium starts cheap and rises with age; a fixed one starts higher and pays off long-term.
strings.n_ins_ltc: Long-term care: check how long it pays (for life or a set period), the waiting period, and whether the premium rises with age.
strings.n_ins_mortlife: Mortgage life: you can buy it outside the bank, usually much cheaper; the bank must accept an outside policy that meets its terms.
strings.n_ins_mortprop: Mortgage property: make sure the sum is the rebuilding cost, not the flat's price.
strings.n_ins_pet: Pet: check exclusions for breed, age and existing conditions.
strings.n_ins_travel: Travel: check pre-existing conditions, extreme sports and luggage; a credit card may include basic cover.
strings.n_jo: Net pay uses 2026 rules, with a 6% employee pension deduction and 2.5% study fund when the employer deposits. A company car adds tax but saves costs, so enter what it saves you. Full package = net + all savings deposits + car and perks.
strings.n_kh: Employees: the employer deposits up to 7.5% and the employee 2.5%, tax-free up to a salary of 15,712 ₪ a month (2026). Self-employed: deduct 4.5% of income up to 13,203 ₪ a year, with capital gains exemption on deposits up to 20,566 ₪. The money is liquid after 6 years (or 3 near retirement age).
strings.n_ks: Bituach Leumi deposits ₪58 a month for every child until 18 (2026), and parents can add another ₪58 from the child allowance. Grants: born before 2017, ₪582 at 18. Born from 2017, ₪291 at 3 and ₪291 at bar/bat mitzvah. Leaving the money until 21 adds another ₪582. Amounts are updated every year, and the return depends on the track.
strings.n_lMode: Calculated by the repayment method you chose (Spitzer, equal principal or balloon).
strings.n_lPrime: Prime = the Bank of Israel rate + the prime spread. Your rate = prime + the bank margin. When the Bank of Israel changes its rate, a prime loan's payment changes.
strings.n_lc: Effective rate uses the net amount after the opening fee and the monthly payments. Assumes an annuity schedule with no indexation.
strings.n_lc2: Stated rate is what the bank quotes. True yearly cost also includes fees and monthly charges, so it is the real price of the loan (also called the effective rate). With the same amount and term, offers are ranked by total cost; otherwise by true yearly cost. Assumes an annuity schedule with no indexation.
strings.n_lcPrime: Prime-based offers assume Prime stays at today's {p}; in practice it moves with the Bank of Israel rate.
strings.n_lcStar: * Rate worked out from the monthly payment you entered.
strings.n_leave: Recuperation days in the private sector: 5 in year 1, 6 in years 2-3, 7 in years 4-10, 8 in 11-15, 9 in 16-19, 10 from year 20, at ₪451.50 a day in 2026. Sick days are not paid out. The divisor and vacation days depend on your contract. Check your contract or the relevant order.
strings.n_lk: Linkage uses the ratio of the two index values. For a binding contract, check the CBS linkage calculator too.
strings.n_lkBuild: The CBS residential construction input index, chained to the latest base. Usually used for payments to a developer on a new home.
strings.n_lkCpi: The CBS general consumer price index, chained to the latest base.
strings.n_lt: 25% on the real gain after expenses and inflation, plus surtax on high income. Residence exemption: if the price exceeds the ceiling, a proportional share is taxed. Eligibility has conditions such as time between sales. An estimate.
strings.n_mc: Annuity per track. CPI-linked tracks grow with the forecast. Excludes life and building insurance. Variable rates will change in practice.
strings.n_mf: Deposit fees come off every deposit, balance fees off everything saved. Legal caps: pension funds up to 6% of deposits and 0.5% of balance; provident and study funds up to 4% and 1.05%. You can ask for a discount or move to a cheaper fund.
strings.n_mortgage: Rates in the form are editable examples, not a bank offer. Bank of Israel limits: financing of 75%, 70% or 50% by buyer type; up to two thirds in variable tracks; payment ratio up to 50%. Purchase tax, insurance and fees are not included.
strings.n_notice: Based on the advance notice law. Days are calendar days. Value is monthly pay times days over 30. A contract may grant more.
strings.n_nw: The stage is approximate: negative worth, non-mortgage debt, cash below 3 months of expenses, passive income below expenses, or fully covered. A mortgage is not treated as costly debt. An estimate, not advice.
strings.n_ot: Under the Hours of Work and Rest Law: a full week is 42 hours and hourly pay is based on 182 hours a month. The first two extra hours a day pay 125%, beyond that 150%. Work on the weekly rest day or a holiday pays at least 150%. Minimum wage from April 2026: 6,443.85 ₪ a month or 35.40 ₪ an hour. Net pay is an estimate.
strings.n_pc: Monthly: return minus savings fee, deposit minus deposit fee. Excludes tax, pension insurance and deposit changes. Past returns don't guarantee future ones.
strings.n_pc_gemel: Provident fund: cap 4% of deposits and 1.05% of savings.
strings.n_pc_hish: Study fund: usually no deposit fee, only on savings.
strings.n_pc_invg: Investment provident fund: yearly deposit cap, withdraw anytime with capital-gains tax.
strings.n_pc_pension: Pension fund: the legal cap is 6% of deposits and 0.5% of savings.
strings.n_pc_policy: Savings policy: check deposit fees and withdrawal penalties too.
strings.n_ph: Official specs and launch prices, checked {d}. There is no public live source for Israeli phone prices, so the local price is what you type. Unpublished figures are marked.
strings.n_points: Child points are counted per parent under 2026 rules; if both parents work, check how points are split between you. A resident man starts at 2.25 points and a woman at 2.75.
strings.n_pp: Prepaying is a safe return equal to the loan rate. Investing carries risk and returns are not guaranteed. A prepayment fee can be added under advanced options; indexation is not included.
strings.n_ppShort: When shortening, the payment stays the same; once the loan ends, the whole payment is invested.
strings.n_prDep: A prime-linked deposit rate moves with the BoI rate. This assumes it stays the same.
strings.n_prLoan: Calculated on the nominal rate ÷ 12, as banks do. With an annuity the payment is recalculated when the rate changes. Excludes indexation, fees and insurance.
strings.n_prOd: An estimate for a constant overdraft. Banks actually charge on the daily balance, usually quarterly.
strings.n_prSimple: Simple interest is on the principal only; compound interest also earns on accrued interest.
strings.n_pt: Brackets reflect early 2026 per public sources and are updated periodically. Check the Tax Authority simulator before a deal. Special reliefs, such as for disabled buyers, are not included.
strings.n_rb: Whoever pays less each month invests the difference at your stated return. Investment tax, land tax and rate changes are not included. The result is very sensitive to the price and rent assumptions.
strings.n_refi: Compares remaining payments on the current loan with payments plus costs on the new one. Indexed or variable loans can change. Differences in term are not adjusted.
strings.n_rental: Full exemption up to ₪5,654 a month. Between ₪5,654 and ₪11,308 the exemption shrinks, and above ₪11,308 there is none. The 10% track is a final tax on gross rent with no deductions. In the regular track rent is added to your other income. Tracks are not available in every case, for example with several rented properties. Check with the Tax Authority.
strings.n_rt: Assumes a constant return and inflation, both of which vary in practice. Income is drawn until the planning age. Tax on pension or withdrawals is not included.
strings.n_sCar: Work car: the 2026 benefit value is 2.48% of the list price a month (up to a price cap of ₪596,860), minus the hybrid, plug-in or electric reduction and minus your contribution. It never reaches your bank account, but you pay income tax, National Insurance and health tax on it.
strings.n_sCarBr: The benefit sits on top of your pay, so it is taxed at your highest brackets. 2026 brackets: 10% up to ₪7,010, 14% up to ₪10,060, 20% up to ₪19,000, 31% up to ₪25,100, 35% up to ₪46,690 and 47% above.
strings.n_salary: Estimate for a resident employee: 2026 tax brackets, National Insurance and health tax, and a 35% credit on the employee pension contribution. It excludes other benefits such as children, qualifying localities or employer study fund contributions. Employer cost assumes 6.5% pension and 6% severance.
strings.n_salary2: An estimate for a resident employee: 2026 brackets, National Insurance and health (1.04% and 3.23% up to ₪7,703; 7% and 5.17% up to ₪51,910) and a 35% credit on the employee pension deposit. Employer deposits above the tax-free limits (pension above 7.5% of ₪33,290, severance above 8.33% of ₪44,100, study fund above 7.5% of ₪15,712) are added as income. A bonus is spread as a monthly average, so the result is close to, but not the same as, the payslip in the month the bonus is paid.
strings.n_selfemp: The self-employed pay National Insurance and health: 7.7% up to ₪7,703 a month and 18% up to ₪51,910. As Bituach Leumi does, the base is the income after deducting 52% of the National Insurance part (not health) and the pension deduction, and never below ₪3,442 a month. The same 52% of the National Insurance part only is also deducted from taxable income. Pension: a 35% credit on up to 5.5% of qualifying income and a deduction of up to 11%, up to a ₪232,800 ceiling. Advances, adjustments and a company comparison are not included.
strings.n_sev: Calculated as last salary times years. The exemption is the lower of last salary and the ceiling, times years. Spreading is approximated at one year per year of service up to 6. Rules differ if funds were deposited in a provident fund. An estimate, not tax advice.
strings.n_sg: Deposits at the end of each month, interest compounded monthly. Returns are not guaranteed.
strings.n_sp: Income-based splitting is proportional to each person’s income.
strings.n_sp2: Split equally, by income, percentages, parts or by what each ordered. Settle up works out who pays whom so everyone pays the same.
strings.n_spx: Amounts are converted to the settling currency at your chosen rate, with the fee. Payments already in that currency have no fee.
strings.n_ss: Safety first: an emergency fund of 3–6 months of needs before risky investing. Compounding does most of the work in later years – so start early. Returns are not guaranteed; not investment advice.
strings.n_tax: Income tax on earned income by 2026 brackets. The surtax is 3% on the part above ₪721,560 a year. Amounts are in shekels regardless of the display currency.
strings.n_tax2: Income tax on earned income by 2026 brackets. Surtax: 3% on all income above ₪721,560 a year, plus 2% on the capital part of it. The pension credit is 35% on up to 7% of income, up to a ceiling.
strings.n_tr: An estimate only, using the 2026 tax brackets and credit points. You can claim a refund for the last 6 years with form 135 or in the Tax Authority personal area. Common reasons: working part of the year, several employers, donations, children, a degree and reserve duty.
strings.n_up: The price is worked out per kilo, liter or unit, including multipacks, so different sizes can be compared.
strings.n_upMix: Items in different measures (weight, volume or units) are compared only within the same group.
strings.n_vat: Rates for other countries are standard rates, for illustration. Israel's rate is 18% since January 2025.
strings.n_wd: Israeli rest days counted as holidays: Rosh Hashanah (2), Yom Kippur, Sukkot, Simchat Torah, Passover (first and seventh), Shavuot and Independence Day. Holiday eves, intermediate days and election days are not counted, so check your work agreement.
strings.note: Calculations are for illustration only and are not financial or tax advice. Tax and wage data are for Israel, 2026. Exchange rates are for reference only, not transaction rates.

strings.pm_noRes: There are no results to explain yet. Open a calculator, enter your numbers, then come back and ask "explain my results".
strings.pm_thanks: You're welcome! I'm here if you have another question.
strings.pm_tip: This is general information, not personal advice. For big decisions, check with an accountant or financial adviser.
strings.pm_unknown: I couldn't find an exact answer to that. Try asking with a term or topic, for example:

strings.pmx_follow: You can follow up, like "and for 10 years?" or "and at 4%?".
strings.pmx_growAsm: You didn't give a return, so I used 5% a year.

strings.pmx_loanNeed: To work out the payment I need an amount and a period, like "a 100k loan for 5 years at 5%".

Hello,

This is the recovery key for the account {n} in the financial calculator:

{c}

To verify the email: type the key in the app, under Settings → Account → Email verification.
Forgot your password? On the sign-in screen tap "Forgot password", type the username and the key, and choose a new password. All data is kept.

strings.lg_a_intro: The financial calculator is meant for everyone, including people with disabilities. It was built as far as possible to WCAG 2.0 level AA and Israeli Standard 5568, and we keep improving it.
strings.lg_a_d1: Screen readers: headings, labels for fields and buttons, and announcements for results that update.
strings.lg_a_d2: Keyboard-only use, with a clear mark of where you are on the screen.
strings.lg_a_d3: High contrast, light or dark colours and a readable font – in Settings → Display & language.
strings.lg_a_d4: Changing text size, and browser zoom up to 200% without losing content.
strings.lg_a_d7: Three languages – Hebrew, Arabic and English – each in its correct direction.
strings.lg_a_d8: Works on phones and small screens, with buttons sized for touch.
strings.lg_a_how: All adjustments are in Settings → Display & language and Settings → Sounds. They are saved on the device and work on every screen.
strings.lg_a_l1: In charts some information is visual. The main values also appear as text or in a table.
strings.lg_a_l2: Content from outside sites, such as the live TradingView board, is not under our control and may not be fully accessible.
strings.lg_a_l3: PDF files the app creates (such as a CV) may not be fully accessible to screen readers.
strings.lg_a_contact: Found an accessibility problem or have a suggestion? Write to us through "Feedback to the developer" in Settings → System, saying which screen and what the problem is. We will look into it and try to fix it soon.
strings.lg_p_intro: The calculator is built so your information stays with you. There are no ads, no tracking or usage statistics, and we do not sell or pass on information to anyone.
strings.lg_p_devH: What is kept on your device
strings.lg_p_dev1: Your settings and the data you enter – in the calculators, CV, accounting and lists – are kept only in your device's browser, in its local storage. The app uses no cookies.
strings.lg_p_dev2: When you sign in, your data is encrypted on the device (AES-GCM, with a key derived from your password). The account itself is local: we have no account server and cannot see your data or recover a password.
strings.lg_p_dev3: A Gemini key, if you saved one, stays only on the device and is left out of exports.
strings.lg_p_us1: Feedback: only what you write in the form and, if you choose, a signed name and/or an e-mail address for a reply. On the website the message is encrypted on your device and sent through a relay service (ntfy.sh), and only the developer can open it. In the Claude app it is kept in the app's database, visible only to the developer.
strings.lg_p_us2: A handle, if you chose one: kept only as a hash, so no one else can take it.
strings.lg_p_us3: Family mode: only a hash of the sign-in is kept, with no names and no list of who is connected.
strings.lg_p_us4: Nothing else is collected: no location, no device model and no usage history.
strings.lg_p_ext0: Requests for prices, rates and fonts go straight from your device, with no cookies and no details about you. A site receiving a request sees your IP address, as with any browsing.
strings.lg_p_ext1: Rates and prices: Bank of Israel, the CBS, CNBC, Coinbase, Binance, Frankfurter and similar sources.
strings.lg_p_ext3: AI, only when you use it: the text you wrote and, when scanning, the photo (a payslip, an offer, an exercise, a letter to translate, or any document with auto-detect) is sent to Claude in the Claude app, or to Google's Gemini with your own key (in developer and family mode). The app does not keep the photo, the letter or the translation; for a payslip only the numbers are kept, on the device. Cover identifying details before taking the photo.
strings.lg_p_ext4: A question to the assistant in an outside service (ChatGPT, Perplexity and the like) opens there only when you choose it.
strings.lg_p_ext5: The live TradingView board loads only when you tap "Show", without telling it which site it is on and without keeping cookies in browsers that support this (such as Chrome).
strings.lg_p_ext6: The website is hosted on GitHub Pages, which sees your IP address each time the site loads, under GitHub's privacy policy.
strings.lg_p_no: No ads, no tracking or analytics tools, no selling information and no profiling.
strings.lg_p_priv: In Settings → Security you can turn on a mode in which the app contacts no outside site. Prices then come from the site's own automatic update.
strings.lg_p_r1: Delete everything on the device: Settings → System → Data and reset, or delete the account in Settings → Account & access.
strings.lg_p_r2: Get a copy of your data: "Backup and restore" in Settings → System.
strings.lg_p_r3: Ask to see, correct or delete feedback you sent: write to us through the feedback form.
strings.lg_p_chg: Whenever we change how information is kept, processed or sent, we will update this document and its date and record the change in the update history at the end.
strings.lg_p_contact: Privacy questions or a request about your information – through "Feedback to the developer" in Settings → System.

strings.lg_p_dev4: The document scanner: a personal card (ID, passport, licence and more) is processed only on the phone – cropping, straightening, hiding details and the watermark – with no AI and nothing sent anywhere, and the scan is not kept in the app. Only the file you chose to download or share remains. strings.sl_h: Photograph the payslip or type its numbers, and the app checks that it adds up, that the tax and National Insurance are right, that your credit points are all there and that the pension meets the law.
strings.sl_priv: The photo goes to the AI only to read the numbers and is not kept. Only the numbers are saved, on your device. You can cover your name, ID number and bank details before taking it.
strings.sl_noAi: Reading a payslip from a photo needs an AI that reads images: it works right away in the Claude app; on the website it needs a Gemini key in Settings.
strings.sl_noAiC: To read a payslip from a photo, allow Claude to read images.
strings.sl_manual: You can also type the payslip numbers yourself – the check itself runs on the device, without AI.
strings.sl_done: Payslip read – check the numbers are right
strings.sl_fail: Could not read the payslip. Try a sharper, straighter photo, or type the numbers.
strings.sl_sumOk: ✅ Nothing unusual found on the payslip
strings.sl_cNoGrossT: Type at least the total gross to check.
strings.sl_cSumOk: Gross {g} minus the deductions comes to exactly the net {n}.
strings.sl_cSumBad: Gross minus the deductions comes to {e}, but the payslip net is {n} – a gap of {x}. An item may not have been read or a deduction is missing; check the fields.
strings.sl_cTaxOk: {a} on the payslip, {b} by the calculation – a match.
strings.sl_cTaxHi: {a} on the payslip, {b} by the calculation – {x} higher. Possible reasons: missing credit points, a second job without tax coordination, or a cumulative adjustment from earlier months.
strings.sl_cTaxLo: {a} on the payslip, {b} by the calculation – {x} lower. This can come from tax coordination, extra credits or a cumulative adjustment; if none apply, you may owe tax at year end.
strings.sl_cPtsAssumed: (Worked out with {p} credit points, as none were entered from the payslip.)
strings.sl_cNiOk: {a} on the payslip, {b} by the calculation – a match.
strings.sl_cNiBad: {a} on the payslip, {b} by the calculation – a gap of {x}. Check the gross and benefits were entered right; if so, ask payroll.
strings.sl_cPtsOk: {a} points – the same as your details in the salary calculator.
strings.sl_cPtsLow: The payslip has {a} points, while your details in the salary calculator give {b}. The gap is worth about {x} a month. If your details are right, give your employer an updated form 101.
strings.sl_cPtsHi: The payslip has {a} points, more than the {b} from your details in the salary calculator. If you are entitled to them, update your details there.
strings.sl_cPtsNone: No credit points were entered from the payslip. They usually appear in the tax details part.
strings.sl_cPensNone: There are no pension deposits. By law the employer must deposit from the seventh month of work, or from the start if you already had a pension fund.
strings.sl_cPensLow: Below the legal minimum: {l}. The percentages are of the basic salary; if deposits are made from a different wage, it may be fine.
strings.sl_cPensOk: Employee {a}, employer {b}, severance {c} of the basic salary – at least the legal minimum.
strings.sl_cSevMiss: No severance deposit is shown. Some payslips leave it out – worth checking in the pension fund report.
strings.sl_cMinT: The basic salary is below the full-time minimum wage ({m}). For part-time work that is fine, as long as the hourly pay is at least {h}.
strings.sl_cBalNeg: There is a negative balance. Check with payroll whether money will be taken off for it.
strings.sl_filled: The numbers were sent to the salary calculator
strings.sl_disc: An estimate based on a simple monthly calculation. Employers sometimes work out tax cumulatively or from details not here, so a small gap is not necessarily a mistake. It does not replace a check by a tax adviser or payroll accountant.

strings.ds_cropH: Drag the four dots to the corners of the card or document. You can also select a dot and move it with the arrow keys.

strings.ds_warnId: Careful: a photo of an ID card, passport or credit card is enough to steal an identity. Send a copy only to a known body that must receive it, hide what is not needed, add a watermark with the purpose, never send it in chats or to someone who contacted you out of the blue, and delete the file from the phone after sending.
strings.ds_warnAi: Do not scan an ID card, passport, credit card or a document with account numbers here – for recognition and translation the photo is sent to the AI. For personal documents choose "Personal card", which works only on the phone.
strings.ds_warnDetCard: This is a personal document. Continue as "Personal card" – from there everything happens only on the phone, without AI.
strings.ds_warnPers: The document seems to show personal details (an ID or account number, an address or medical information). If you continue to translation it is sent to the AI. You can cancel, cover the details and take the photo again.
strings.ds_warnPersL: The letter contains personal details. Share the translation only with whoever needs it, and delete downloaded files when you no longer need them.
strings.ds_warnSend: Before sending: check the recipient is genuine and really needs the copy, and leave visible only what is required.
strings.d_taxfree: Tax on shopping in every country: VAT, US state and Canadian provincial sales tax, and how much comes back with Tax Free – minimums, fees, airport steps and a form ready in the country's language.
strings.tf_verify: The amount changes from time to time – confirm it in the shop.
strings.tf_n_eu: In the EU: for people living outside the EU (Israelis too). Take the goods out of the EU within 3 months of the end of the month of purchase, and have the form validated by customs at the last EU port. The minimum is per receipt from one shop.
strings.tf_n_ot: Usually: ask for a form in the shop, have it validated by customs as you leave the country, and get the refund at a desk or to your card.
strings.tf_n_gb: The UK has had no tourist VAT refund since 2021 (except for goods the shop sends straight abroad).
strings.tf_n_us: The US has no VAT: there is a state and city sales tax, which is not included in the shelf price – it is added at the till. Tourists usually cannot get it back.
strings.tf_n_jp: In Japan the exemption is given in the shop on showing your passport. From 1.11.2026 Japan moves to a refund system: you pay the full price and get the tax back after a check on departure.
strings.tf_n_th: In Thailand: at least 2,000 baht per shop per day and at least 5,000 baht in total for the trip. Have the form validated by customs before check-in.
strings.tf_n_ae: In the UAE: most of the VAT (about 87%) comes back, less a fixed fee per form. Validation is at a kiosk in the airport.
strings.tf_n_au: In Australia (TRS): at least A$300 from one business (several invoices are fine), bought within 60 days before leaving. The full GST comes back at the TRS desk in the airport.
strings.tf_n_il: Tourists only (B2/B3/B4 visa or form 17). Israelis, even with dual citizenship, are not eligible. Minimum ₪186 including VAT, in an approved shop with a sticker, with a tax invoice and a special document of the same date. The refund is at the Milgam desk at Ben Gurion, Ramon or the land crossings – before you leave.
strings.tf_ilFees: Milgam fees: ₪27 per document checked; for cash another 1% + VAT of the refund; by bank transfer ₪47.5 once; by cheque – nothing extra.
strings.tf_itOk: VAT on the receipt {v} · about {n} back
strings.tf_itShort: Below the minimum – {m} more at the same shop
strings.tf_itEmpty: Enter the amount from the receipt.
strings.tf_how: How do you get the refund?
strings.tf_feeH: Refund companies (Global Blue, Planet and the like) keep part of the VAT. The percentage here is an estimate you can change. A refund from the shop itself usually has no fee.
strings.tf_lost: {v} of VAT will not come back because the receipt is below the minimum.
strings.tf_thTotal: In Thailand you need at least 5,000 baht in total to get a refund.
strings.tf_disc: An estimate only: the final amount depends on the shop, the refund company and the exchange rate. Minimums and rates were checked in October 2026.
strings.tf_steps: What to do – step by step
strings.tf_s_1: In the shop: show your passport and ask for a Tax Free form. Details go in Latin letters, as in your passport.
strings.tf_s_2: Keep the receipt, the form and the goods – new, unused, with their tags.
strings.tf_s_3: Get to the airport early. If the goods are in your suitcase – go to customs validation before check-in.
strings.tf_s_eu4: Have the form validated by customs (stamp or digital scan) at the last port where you leave the EU.
strings.tf_s_eu5: The goods must leave the EU within 3 months of the end of the month of purchase.
strings.tf_s_ot4: Have the form validated by customs or at a kiosk as you leave the country.
strings.tf_s_6: Collect the refund at the refund company's desk, or send the form in and get it on your card.
strings.tf_s_il1: Make sure the shop is approved – a sticker on the window or door.
strings.tf_s_il2: Get a tax invoice and the special tourist document, with the same date and all details filled in.
strings.tf_s_il3: At Ben Gurion: if the goods are in your suitcase – go to the Milgam desk at the departure hall entrance, before security.
strings.tf_s_il4: Show your passport, visa or form 17, the goods and the documents.
strings.tf_s_il5: Apply before leaving the country – a request from abroad is not accepted. The refund is paid at the desk after passport control.
strings.tf_s_au1: Buy at least A$300 from one business (incl. GST) within 60 days before your flight and keep the tax invoice.
strings.tf_s_au2: You can lodge it in advance in the TRS app.
strings.tf_s_au3: At the airport: after passport control, at the TRS desk – show the goods, passport, boarding pass and invoices.
strings.tf_s_jp2: In the shop you either pay without tax or get a refund – depending on the system in force on the day of purchase.
strings.tf_s_jp3: On departure show your passport and the goods at customs.
strings.tf_form: Details for the form – in the country's language
strings.tf_formH: Write in your own language and the app prepares the details in Latin letters and in the form's language – to copy or to show the shop assistant.
strings.tf_formWarn: These are personal details. They stay on the phone and are not kept unless you tick "remember". The passport number is not entered here – write it straight on the shop's form.
strings.tf_keep: Remember the details on this device
strings.tf_trGo: Prepare the details for the form
strings.tf_formEmpty: Fill in at least one detail.
strings.tf_offline: Prepared on the phone without AI: names and addresses were turned into Latin letters roughly – correct them to match your passport.
strings.tf_checkPass: The name must match your passport exactly.
strings.tf_n_nz: New Zealand has no GST refund for tourists on shop purchases, except goods the shop sends straight abroad.
strings.tf_n_zero: This country has no general VAT or sales tax on shopping, so there is nothing to get back.
strings.tf_n_unk: We have no verified information about a tourist tax refund in this country. The price usually includes the tax above – ask in the shop whether Tax Free is offered.
strings.tf_n_ca: In Canada tax is not included in the shelf price and is added at the till: federal GST, and in some provinces a provincial tax too (or a combined HST). There has been no general visitor refund since 2007.
strings.tf_approx: This is the standard rate; some goods have a reduced rate, and it may change.
strings.tf_locH: The default is the state's average local rate (Tax Foundation, 1.7.2026). If you know your city's rate, type it in.
strings.tf_stDisc: An estimate: some goods (such as food or clothing in some states) are exempt or taxed differently, and some cities add extra taxes.
